freshness.note: Joint game simulation: team volume, each player's share of it, then efficiency measured from 10,000 deterministic iterations.

simulationSummary.headline: DEN @ ATL: 139 player markets simulated over 10,000 deterministic iterations each.

winProbability.calibration: Shrunk toward 50% by a factor fit before testing (λ=0.25).

keyNumbers.note: Share of simulated margins landing exactly on the numbers football scoring piles up on.

overtimeProbability.note: Share of simulated games tied at the end of regulation. Preseason overtime rules vary, so this is the tie share, not a resolved overtime winner.

periodMarkets.reason: Quarter and half lines need measured per-period scoring. Our corpus carries final scores only, so publishing a split would mean inventing the shares it rests on.
periodMarkets.whatWouldChangeIt: a per-quarter scoring corpus, which is the same missing ingredient as drive-level data.

simulationSummary.readinessNote: This model has no measurable read on which of these two teams is better in preseason: the coefficient linking team strength to margin is indistinguishable from zero (t = -0.5746, 95% interval [-0.077667,0.042782]). Rather than publish a direction it cannot support, the team term is set to zero, so this forecast reflects preseason scoring and home context only.

unavailableModules.displayCopy: No sportsbook offers NFL player markets for this game, so there is no price to compare our projections against. We do not invent one.
First and last touchdown need drive ordering. Our corpus carries per-game stat lines with no ordering, so the mechanism does not exist.
Scoreline distributions are a soccer module.

freshness.note: Joint game simulation: team volume, each player's share of it, then efficiency measured from 10,000 deterministic iterations.

simulationSummary.headline: TB @ NYJ: 139 player markets simulated over 10,000 deterministic iterations each.

winProbability.calibration: Shrunk toward 50% by a factor fit before testing (λ=0.25).

keyNumbers.note: Share of simulated margins landing exactly on the numbers football scoring piles up on.

overtimeProbability.note: Share of simulated games tied at the end of regulation. Preseason overtime rules vary, so this is the tie share, not a resolved overtime winner.

periodMarkets.reason: Quarter and half lines need measured per-period scoring. Our corpus carries final scores only, so publishing a split would mean inventing the shares it rests on.
periodMarkets.whatWouldChangeIt: a per-quarter scoring corpus, which is the same missing ingredient as drive-level data.

simulationSummary.readinessNote: This model has no measurable read on which of these two teams is better in preseason: the coefficient linking team strength to margin is indistinguishable from zero (t = -0.5746, 95% interval [-0.077667,0.042782]). Rather than publish a direction it cannot support, the team term is set to zero, so this forecast reflects preseason scoring and home context only.

unavailableModules.displayCopy: No sportsbook offers NFL player markets for this game, so there is no price to compare our projections against. We do not invent one.

Scoreline distributions are a soccer module.

freshness.note: Joint game simulation: team volume, each player's share of it, then efficiency measured from 10,000 deterministic iterations.

simulationSummary.headline: MIA @ WSH: 111 player markets simulated over 10,000 deterministic iterations each.

winProbability.calibration: Shrunk toward 50% by a factor fit before testing (λ=0.25).

keyNumbers.note: Share of simulated margins landing exactly on the numbers football scoring piles up on.

overtimeProbability.note: Share of simulated games tied at the end of regulation. Preseason overtime rules vary, so this is the tie share, not a resolved overtime winner.

periodMarkets.reason: Quarter and half lines need measured per-period scoring. Our corpus carries final scores only, so publishing a split would mean inventing the shares it rests on.
periodMarkets.whatWouldChangeIt: a per-quarter scoring corpus, which is the same missing ingredient as drive-level data.

simulationSummary.readinessNote: This model has no measurable read on which of these two teams is better in preseason: the coefficient linking team strength to margin is indistinguishable from zero (t = -0.5746, 95% interval [-0.077667,0.042782]). Rather than publish a direction it cannot support, the team term is set to zero, so this forecast reflects preseason scoring and home context only.

unavailableModules.displayCopy: No sportsbook offers NFL player markets for this game, so there is no price to compare our projections against. We do not invent one.
First and last touchdown need drive ordering. Our corpus carries per-game stat lines with no ordering, so the mechanism does not exist.
Scoreline distributions are a soccer module.

freshness.note: Joint game simulation: team volume, each player's share of it, then efficiency measured from 10,000 deterministic iterations.

simulationSummary.headline: CAR @ BUF: 142 player markets simulated over 10,000 deterministic iterations each.

winProbability.calibration: Shrunk toward 50% by a factor fit before testing (λ=0.25).

keyNumbers.note: Share of simulated margins landing exactly on the numbers football scoring piles up on.

overtimeProbability.note: Share of simulated games tied at the end of regulation. Preseason overtime rules vary, so this is the tie share, not a resolved overtime winner.

periodMarkets.reason: Quarter and half lines need measured per-period scoring. Our corpus carries final scores only, so publishing a split would mean inventing the shares it rests on.
periodMarkets.whatWouldChangeIt: a per-quarter scoring corpus, which is the same missing ingredient as drive-level data.

simulationSummary.readinessNote: This model has no measurable read on which of these two teams is better in preseason: the coefficient linking team strength to margin is indistinguishable from zero (t = -0.5746, 95% interval [-0.077667,0.042782]). Rather than publish a direction it cannot support, the team term is set to zero, so this forecast reflects preseason scoring and home context only.

unavailableModules.displayCopy: No sportsbook offers NFL player markets for this game, so there is no price to compare our projections against. We do not invent one.
First and last touchdown need drive ordering. Our corpus carries per-game stat lines with no ordering, so the mechanism does not exist.
Scoreline distributions are a soccer module.

freshness.note: Joint game simulation: team volume, each player's share of it, then efficiency measured from 10,000 deterministic iterations.

simulationSummary.headline: CLE @ CHI: 159 player markets simulated over 10,000 deterministic iterations each.

winProbability.calibration: Shrunk toward 50% by a factor fit before testing (λ=0.25).

keyNumbers.note: Share of simulated margins landing exactly on the numbers football scoring piles up on.

overtimeProbability.note: Share of simulated games tied at the end of regulation. Preseason overtime rules vary, so this is the tie share, not a resolved overtime winner.

periodMarkets.reason: Quarter and half lines need measured per-period scoring. Our corpus carries final scores only, so publishing a split would mean inventing the shares it rests on.
periodMarkets.whatWouldChangeIt: a per-quarter scoring corpus, which is the same missing ingredient as drive-level data.

simulationSummary.readinessNote: This model has no measurable read on which of these two teams is better in preseason: the coefficient linking team strength to margin is indistinguishable from zero (t = -0.5746, 95% interval [-0.077667,0.042782]). Rather than publish a direction it cannot support, the team term is set to zero, so this forecast reflects preseason scoring and home context only.

unavailableModules.displayCopy: No sportsbook offers NFL player markets for this game, so there is no price to compare our projections against. We do not invent one.
First and last touchdown need drive ordering. Our corpus carries per-game stat lines with no ordering, so the mechanism does not exist.
Scoreline distributions are a soccer module.

freshness.note: Joint game simulation: team volume, each player's share of it, then efficiency measured from 10,000 deterministic iterations.

simulationSummary.headline: MIN @ NYG: 148 player markets simulated over 10,000 deterministic iterations each.

winProbability.calibration: Shrunk toward 50% by a factor fit before testing (λ=0.25).

keyNumbers.note: Share of simulated margins landing exactly on the numbers football scoring piles up on.

overtimeProbability.note: Share of simulated games tied at the end of regulation. Preseason overtime rules vary, so this is the tie share, not a resolved overtime winner.

periodMarkets.reason: Quarter and half lines need measured per-period scoring. Our corpus carries final scores only, so publishing a split would mean inventing the shares it rests on.
periodMarkets.whatWouldChangeIt: a per-quarter scoring corpus, which is the same missing ingredient as drive-level data.

simulationSummary.readinessNote: This model has no measurable read on which of these two teams is better in preseason: the coefficient linking team strength to margin is indistinguishable from zero (t = -0.5746, 95% interval [-0.077667,0.042782]). Rather than publish a direction it cannot support, the team term is set to zero, so this forecast reflects preseason scoring and home context only.

unavailableModules.displayCopy: No sportsbook offers NFL player markets for this game, so there is no price to compare our projections against. We do not invent one.
First and last touchdown need drive ordering. Our corpus carries per-game stat lines with no ordering, so the mechanism does not exist.
Scoreline distributions are a soccer module.

freshness.note: Joint game simulation: team volume, each player's share of it, then efficiency measured from 10,000 deterministic iterations.

simulationSummary.headline: LAR @ KC: 122 player markets simulated over 10,000 deterministic iterations each.

winProbability.calibration: Shrunk toward 50% by a factor fit before testing (λ=0.25).

keyNumbers.note: Share of simulated margins landing exactly on the numbers football scoring piles up on.

overtimeProbability.note: Share of simulated games tied at the end of regulation. Preseason overtime rules vary, so this is the tie share, not a resolved overtime winner.

periodMarkets.reason: Quarter and half lines need measured per-period scoring. Our corpus carries final scores only, so publishing a split would mean inventing the shares it rests on.
periodMarkets.whatWouldChangeIt: a per-quarter scoring corpus, which is the same missing ingredient as drive-level data.

freshness.note: Joint game simulation: team volume, each player's share of it, then efficiency measured from 10,000 deterministic iterations.

simulationSummary.headline: JAX @ NO: 157 player markets simulated over 10,000 deterministic iterations each.

winProbability.calibration: Shrunk toward 50% by a factor fit before testing (λ=0.25).

keyNumbers.note: Share of simulated margins landing exactly on the numbers football scoring piles up on.

overtimeProbability.note: Share of simulated games tied at the end of regulation. Preseason overtime rules vary, so this is the tie share, not a resolved overtime winner.

periodMarkets.reason: Quarter and half lines need measured per-period scoring. Our corpus carries final scores only, so publishing a split would mean inventing the shares it rests on.
periodMarkets.whatWouldChangeIt: a per-quarter scoring corpus, which is the same missing ingredient as drive-level data.

simulationSummary.readinessNote: This model has no measurable read on which of these two teams is better in preseason: the coefficient linking team strength to margin is indistinguishable from zero (t = -0.5746, 95% interval [-0.077667,0.042782]). unavailableModules.displayCopy: No sportsbook offers NFL player markets for this game, so there is no price to compare our projections against. We do not invent one.
First and last touchdown need drive ordering. Our corpus carries per-game stat lines with no ordering, so the mechanism does not exist.
Scoreline distributions are a soccer module.

freshness.note: Joint game simulation: team volume, each player's share of it, then efficiency measured from 10,000 deterministic iterations.

simulationSummary.headline: PHI @ BAL: 120 player markets simulated over 10,000 deterministic iterations each.

winProbability.calibration: Shrunk toward 50% by a factor fit before testing (λ=0.25).

keyNumbers.note: Share of simulated margins landing exactly on the numbers football scoring piles up on.

overtimeProbability.note: Share of simulated games tied at the end of regulation. Preseason overtime rules vary, so this is the tie share, not a resolved overtime winner.

periodMarkets.reason: Quarter and half lines need measured per-period scoring. Our corpus carries final scores only, so publishing a split would mean inventing the shares it rests on.
periodMarkets.whatWouldChangeIt: a per-quarter scoring corpus, which is the same missing ingredient as drive-level data.

simulationSummary.readinessNote: This model has no measurable read on which of these two teams is better in preseason: the coefficient linking team strength to margin is indistinguishable from zero (t = -0.5746, 95% interval [-0.077667,0.042782]). Rather than publish a direction it cannot support, the team term is set to zero, so this forecast reflects preseason scoring and home context only.

unavailableModules.displayCopy: No sportsbook offers NFL player markets for this game, so there is no price to compare our projections against. We do not invent one.
First and last touchdown need drive ordering. Our corpus carries per-game stat lines with no ordering, so the mechanism does not exist.
Scoreline distributions are a soccer module.

freshness.note: Joint game simulation: team volume, each player's share of it, then efficiency measured from 10,000 deterministic iterations.

simulationSummary.headline: DAL @ SEA: 167 player markets simulated over 10,000 deterministic iterations each.

winProbability.calibration: Shrunk toward 50% by a factor fit before testing (λ=0.25).

keyNumbers.note: Share of simulated margins landing exactly on the numbers football scoring piles up on.

overtimeProbability.note: Share of simulated games tied at the end of regulation. Preseason overtime rules vary, so this is the tie share, not a resolved overtime winner.

periodMarkets.reason: Quarter and half lines need measured per-period scoring. Our corpus carries final scores only, so publishing a split would mean inventing the shares it rests on.
periodMarkets.whatWouldChangeIt: a per-quarter scoring corpus, which is the same missing ingredient as drive-level data.

simulationSummary.readinessNote: This model has no measurable read on which of these two teams is better in preseason: the coefficient linking team strength to margin is indistinguishable from zero (t = -0.5746, 95% interval [-0.077667,0.042782]). Rather than publish a direction it cannot support, the team term is set to zero, so this forecast reflects preseason scoring and home context only.

unavailableModules.displayCopy: No sportsbook offers NFL player markets for this game, so there is no price to compare our projections against. We do not invent one.
First and last touchdown need drive ordering. Our corpus carries per-game stat lines with no ordering, so the mechanism does not exist.
Scoreline distributions are a soccer module.

honesty.teamModel: the team score distribution is BASELINE_ONLY — no measured signal separates these teams, so it reflects league-wide preseason context and home field only.
honesty.playerModel: player distributions come from a joint simulation of team opportunity, participation share and preseason efficiency measured from 739 passing / 1,817 rushing / 3,768 receiving preseason player-games. They are RESEARCH ESTIMATES: none of the four families beat a simple role baseline when tested, and the ranges are wide because preseason playing time genuinely is.
honesty.market: team markets carry a real captured line and a real comparison. Player markets are not offered by the provider for these games, so player rows carry model probability only and no line is invented.
honesty.notAdvice: educational and paper-only; not betting advice, and not shown to beat the market.
